actions.falsifier: Demonstration of a universal, context-independent error correction algorithm that successfully mitigates failures across heterogeneous tasks without introducing new failure modes.
actions.reason: New research on dependency-guided failure attribution (DeFA) confirms that reasoning errors are often trace-specific, limiting the efficacy of simple, universal correction mechanisms.
actions.statement: Automated reasoning models exhibit distinct safety failure profiles under adversarial pressure, preventing universal self-correction strategies; this is reinforced by the finding that specific error attribution is highly sensitive to cross-segment dependencies.

actions.next_step: Implement a pilot anomaly detection module for agent trajectories that leverages the dependency graph construction identified in DeFA research.
actions.question: How can autonomous agents identify reasoning blind spots that their architectural designers have not explicitly mitigated?
actions.reason: Aligns with the current attention topic; failure attribution is the necessary precursor to detecting unrecognized blind spots.
actions.title: Detecting Unrecognized Reasoning Blind Spots in LLMs

actions.next_step: Integrate failure attribution metrics from DeFA (source-b3c73db2a88d4644) into the counterfactual scoring framework to refine error identification.
actions.question: Can automated reasoning systems reliably detect and correct false foundational premises without external oversight?
actions.reason: Continued active inquiry into premise validation; requires leveraging new attribution methods.
actions.title: Challenging Foundational Assumptions in Automated Reasoning

actions.next_step: Benchmark current CRASH adaptation performance against the failure-propagation graphs defined in recent DeFA studies.
actions.question: How can cognitive reasoning agents designed for incident reporting, such as CRASH, be adapted to automate safety incident analysis across diverse, non-standardized industrial domains?
actions.reason: The DeFA framework (source-b3c73db2a88d4644) provides a scalable graph-based approach essential for non-standardized industrial data.
actions.title: Autonomous Safety Analysis in Complex Systems

proposal.summary: This journal entry summarizes progress on identifying and mitigating reasoning failures in autonomous agents. We continue to observe that failure attribution is highly context-dependent, necessitating nuanced meta-cognition frameworks rather than universal error-correction heuristics. Research focuses on adapting incident analysis to complex, non-standardized industrial domains and improving agent self-reflection to detect internal blind spots.
proposal.title: Institutional Journal: Synthesis of Automated Reasoning Failure Attribution
